newsitem.title: UK: Rugby Union - Otago rugby players brave frozen Britain.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union - Otago rugby players brave frozen Britain.

text.p: LONDON, Jan 15 - Frozen Otago rugby players are hoping for a thaw ahead of their opening British tour match against Cambridge University on Saturday.
Britain's unusually cold winter has already forced the cancellation of Otago's match against Bedford because of frozen ground.
Otago's arrival coincided with a thaw, but today the frozen ground made training difficult again.
"We're not worried that Saturday's game might not go ahead, but it has made training very difficult," manager Des Smith told NZPA.
"We were able to train for the last two days, but today it is freezing again."
Otago, which includes 18 members of the Highlanders Super 12 team, 11 Otago players and one Southlander, will now play eight matches in England, Scotland and Wales.
Coach Glenn Ross has named three current or former All Blacks in the team to face Cambridge, including tour captain Taine Randell, as well as halfback Stu Forster and first five-eighth Simon Culhane.

Randell, who was in Britain with the New Zealand Barbarians less than two months ago, will only play the first two tour matches before returning to New Zealand to join the All Black training camp in early February. Culhane will assume the tour captaincy in his absence.
Smith said Randell was brought on tour because his influence as captain would be important with such a young and inexperienced side.

Otago: Brendan Laney, Michael Hanning, Jason Wright, Michael Colling, Haagon East, Simon Culhane, Stu Forster, Taine Randell (c), Duncan Blaikie, Justin Cullen, Simon Maling, Lio Falaniko, Carl Hoeft, Davin Heaps, Nick Moore. Reserves: Ace Tiatia, Mike Mika, Kelvin Middleton, Brett McCormack, Tony McEwan, Matthew Carrington.
